id_and_class.theory_title: Pauli’s One World, Two Aspects: Psychophysical Complementarity
id_and_class.summary: Wolfgang Pauli held that mind and matter are complementary aspects of one underlying reality, the unus mundus (‘one world’), which is itself neither mental nor physical and cannot be observed directly. Conscious experience is the subjective pole of that split, and archetypes act as ordering principles that shape both psyche and physical nature.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Psychic Aspect of One World

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is one of two complementary aspects of a psychophysically neutral, archetypally ordered reality. Phenomenal experience and physical process are equally real and equally derivative.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mind and matter arise through an epistemic split of an undivided whole. Pauli treats them as complementary in Bohr's sense: mutually exclusive, jointly necessary descriptions, neither reducible to the other.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (mind and matter result from the decomposition of an undivided neutral whole, so consciousness neither emerges from matter nor is the foundation of it)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjectivity is the psychic pole of the split. The observing psyche cannot be removed from what it observes, so becoming aware of an unconscious content irreversibly changes it, much as measurement disturbs a quantum system.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Pauli offers no separate account of qualia. Because the explanatory gap follows from the split itself, he treats it as a structural feature of reality, not a defect in any particular theory.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: The unus mundus as a holistic, psychophysically neutral reality; archetypes as neutral ordering principles; a collective unconscious as an objective level of mind; physical systems described by quantum theory.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: The neutral ground is inaccessible in principle and is the condition of knowledge, not its object. Its two aspects are known through physics on one side and introspection, dreams and depth psychology on the other.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: An undivided whole, split epistemically into a mental and a physical aspect, with archetypes producing structured correlations between them. Pauli's quaternio pairs energy and space-time with causality and synchronicity.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal experience, the conscious-unconscious relation, scientific concept formation, and mind-matter correlations including synchronicity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Complementarity extended from quantum physics to psychology, combined with archetypes as psychophysically neutral ordering operators that Pauli described as statistical laws with primary probabilities.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Mental and physical aspects appear when the undivided whole is partitioned in the act of knowing. Becoming conscious of an unconscious content is itself a dynamic, irreversible change in that content.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Consciousness is not located in the brain alone. It is the subjective aspect of a reality whose neutral ground lies outside space and time as we observe them.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Ordinary mind-matter regularities come from archetypal ordering. Pauli and Jung also posited synchronicity, acausal but meaningful coincidences, and Pauli speculated about a law of nature grounded in meaning rather than in cause.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Unity comes first: the neutral reality is whole before any split into mental and physical, so the problem is how it divides, not how parts combine.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Archetypes bridge sense perception and concept formation. Pauli argued in his Kepler essay that archetypal images shaped scientific theory, which would explain why mathematics conceived in the mind fits nature.
core_claims_and_evidence: Pauli holds that mind and matter are two complementary aspects of one psychophysically neutral reality, the unus mundus.
Becoming conscious of an unconscious content alters it, which Pauli compares to measurement disturbing a quantum system.
Archetypes order both psyche and matter, and Pauli cited Kepler's use of archetypal images to explain the fit between mathematics and nature.
Synchronicities are rare, meaningful, acausal coincidences that Pauli treated as special cases of more general acausal dispositions.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Speculative and philosophical, drawing on quantum theory, Jungian depth psychology, dream analysis and the history of science.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Because the neutral domain is inaccessible in principle, the view resists direct test and risks explanatory emptiness. The archetypes it relies on are formally underspecified, and the synchronicity component, on which Pauli placed considerable weight, is empirically contested.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Whether an undivided neutral reality explains phenomenal consciousness or only renames the mystery at a deeper level. Most of the view survives in correspondence, and the formal versions are reconstructions by Atmanspacher, Primas and colleagues.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a dual-aspect position that rejects both materialism and idealism. It differs from the neutral monism of Mach, James and Russell by treating the neutral ground as an undivided whole that cannot serve as a set of accessible building blocks.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Pauli speculated about a law of nature grounded in meaning and saw archetypes ordering both mind and matter, which gives meaning a place in nature beyond human concerns.
